says: In next/, every jobs.list reads every target: line the key ever got and then each named job's whole stream, finished ones included, so one list grows with the key's lifetime, not with its open work.
proof: JobsLedger.ts:205-212, forTarget reads turn.read(index, 0) from rev 0 and calls saved(turn, id) for each pointer before it filters to open jobs.
cost: A key that ran thousands of jobs pays thousands of stream reads on every list, inside the write turn, and the client lists after every job and every wake.
